blocks.text: Ceramic vessels at the entrance to a cave passage near San Ignacio, Belize
San Ignacio, Belize: clay vessels among rocks in a cave

Caracol lies high on the Vaca Plateau, deep in the Chiquibul Forest Reserve. It is the largest Maya city in Belize and was rediscovered in 1936.

Caracol covers more than 80 square miles and contains about 30,000 structures. At its peak, more than 150,000 people lived here. The settlement sits about 1,600 feet above sea level, with no natural body of water nearby. Access to very hard stone and copal, both prized by the Maya, may explain the choice of site.

At the centre stands the massive Caana pyramid, also known as Sky Palace. It has been almost fully restored and stands more than 135 feet tall. From the top, you can look out across the forested mountains.

On the early drive to Caracol, you may see tapirs, jaguars or ocelots. Huge ceiba, mahogany and sapodilla trees grow at the site. It is a good place to watch for birds, including the rare keel-billed motmot, as well as howler monkeys, spider monkeys and grey foxes.

After the tour, return to the hotel in the afternoon.

Overnight in San Ignacio at Midas Resort.
